text:
maria: quick thread — i'm prototyping an 'accounting_envelope' that rides with metering/billing events. goal: single canonical record we can use for audits, cost-forwarding, and recons without touching raw payloads. want thoughts on minimal fields and tradeoffs.

jay: love it. does envelope mean we duplicate data (model, tokens) or we just point to the original event?

maria: ideally minimal duplication. pointer to raw ingest offset + denormalized small fields (token counts, model id, cost_nanos) so reconciles are cheap. big tradeoff is late-arrival handling.

oliver: pointer-only + occasional denorm is fine if pointer is stable. we need a deterministic canonicalization process so backfills produce same accounting values as live path. that implies we store model checksum or version in the envelope.

kat: late arrivals are killer. if an event arrives after billing window, do we emit a delta event or mutate prior aggregates? both have accounting/legal implications. we should prefer emitting correction events with a clear "correction_of" pointer.

anita: +1 to corrections. also, auditability requires immutability on raw events. we should never rewrite raw ingest — only emit new correction events. customer invoices should be derived from the reconciliation job that consumes envelopes and applies ordered corrections.

ricardo: how do we compute cost deterministically? quantization/optimizer changes can change token cost. proposal: cost_nanos in envelope is the computed price at time of accounting, and we also store pricing_policy_id used. then reconciliation can show diffs if pricing changes.

maria: exactly. sample envelope sketch (pseudo):

```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01H...",
  "provenance": { "source": "ingest_v2", "kafka_offset": "topic-4:12345" },
  "attribution": { "account_id": "acct_123", "api_key_id": "key_abc", "route": "/v1/generate" },
  "model": { "id": "redwood-13b-v1", "model_checksum": "sha256:..." },
  "tokens": { "input": 72, "output": 184 },
  "cost_nanos": 1540000000,
  "pricing_policy_id": "pp-2026-03-01",
  "accounting_version": "1",
  "correction_of": null
}
```

jay: nice. a few concerns: 1) events can be huge at peak, we can't store full denorm per event for every request. 2) indexing offsets for provenance at exabyte scale.

oliver: for (1) we only denorm the small fields. raw text/inputs must not be duplicated. we already have object storage for raw payloads and a pointer here. for (2) provenance should be a compact pointer: (topic, partition, offset) + checksum. keep it tiny.

kat: re: corrections, we need conventions: correction events must include a signed delta (tokens_delta, cost_delta) and a reconciler id and timestamp. that allows ledger-style audit trails.

anita: operational flow proposal: ingest -> raw store + minimal event to events-kafka -> accounting-enricher consumes, emits accounting_envelope into accounting-topic -> reconciler consumes accounting-topic, writes time-series aggregates + ledger entries. reconciler can also emit correction events if upstream repairs happen.

ricardo: question: how do we support multi-route attributions (function calling, tool-calls) where one LLM call spawns multiple billable micro-calls? should envelope be per top-level request or per billable subcall?

maria: i'd advocate per billable primitive (atomic token-charge). then we can glue them to top-level via session_id and parent_event_id. This simplifies unit accounting and routing-based discounts.

jay: testing/backfill: we need a replayable deterministic pipeline. keep enrichment logic in a library we can run in backfill mode. avoid opaque SQL in the reconciler. also log the library version in envelope.

oliver: SLA implications: Dedicated/private customers may expect different attribution rules. include origin enum (hosted|dedicated|private) and tenant_config_version that captures any billing overrides.

kat: monitoring: add lightweight sanity metrics: envelope_count, correction_count, median-lag (ingest->envelope), reconciliation_fail_rate. dashboards + alert when corrections spike.

maria: next steps i'll draft short RFC with: envelope schema, correction protocol, backfill tooling, reconciler contract, example queries for invoices. will include a compatibility plan for schema evolution (accounting_version + wire compatibility).

ricardo: please include migration strategy for old events: can we enrich them lazily? full backfill is expensive. propose: opportunistic enrichment on read + background backfill for high-traffic tenants.

anita: agree. also add governance: who can mark an event as corrected? require approval or signed job id for automated repairs.

sre-bot: deploy-notice: accounting-enricher v2 will roll out to canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC. monitor corrections metric. :rotating_light:

maria: thanks all — i'll post RFC link once drafted. if anyone wants to pair on the backfill plan ping me. :thumbsup:
